title: String Length — original explanatory diagram
author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. Conceptual open and closed strings, not a photograph, measured geometry, physical cord, or fixed universal string-length prediction. No numerical string/Planck equivalence is asserted.

title: Carbon Atom — original explanatory diagram
author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. 140 pm is twice the tabulated 70 pm empirical atomic radius. Cloud/lobes are qualitative, not an ab initio density, enclosed-probability contour or literal surface. Nucleus enlarged.

title: Hyperion — original explanatory diagram
author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. Guinness reports Hyperion at 116.07 m in 2019, rounded here to approximately 116 m. Original generic coast-redwood silhouette, not a verified photograph or reconstruction of its crown. Does not corroborate the dataset’s unsourced 116.2 m / 2026 claim.

title: Longest Lightning Flash — original explanatory diagram
author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. WMO reports 829 ± 8 km for the 22 October 2017 US megaflash, measured by maximum great-circle separation. Authored channels/clouds are conceptual, not satellite data or traced channel geometry.

title: Kuiper Belt — original explanatory diagram
author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. NASA places the main belt at approximately 30–50 AU, hence approximately 100 AU outer diameter. Original face-on annulus is a regional schematic, with no synthetic catalog points. Band edges are approximate and do not delimit all trans-Neptunian objects.

title: Hercules-Corona Borealis Great Wall — original explanatory diagram
author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. The paper reports 14 of 31 GRBs at 1.6 < z < 2.1 in roughly 1/8 of the sky and infers a 2000–3000 Mpc span. A simple count strip conveys those published counts, not measured angular positions, structure membership or a mapped boundary. The proposed wall is explicitly disputed; no galaxy-wall artwork is copied.

title: DVD Track Pitch — original explanatory diagram
author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. ECMA-267 specifies a 0.74 µm nominal track pitch (±0.03 µm). Parallel strips are a locally straightened view of adjacent spiral turns; drawn mark widths, lengths and sequence are illustrative, not a micrograph or encoded data.

title: Prelude FLNG — original explanatory diagram
author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. Shell states 488 m length and 74 m width. The bounding hull proportions follow those dimensions; hull contours and generic equipment symbols are original illustrative design, not a traced Shell rendering, photograph or as-built deck layout. No qualifying facility photo was established in the prior images3 search.

title: Danyang-Kunshan Grand Bridge — original explanatory diagram
author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. The opened Guinness record page gives the bridge length rounded to 164 km; this image uses that coarse figure rather than claiming the page states 164.8 km. The ruler represents total length, while the generic viaduct segment and train are illustrative, not a route map, engineering elevation or claim that the pictured segment spans 164 km. Prior images3 photo candidates were BY-SA or all rights reserved.

title: Credit Card — original explanatory diagram
author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. ID-1 length 85.60 mm and width 53.98 mm. Original unbranded card with generic chip motif; no actual account, personal data, company logo or copied card design. Corner shape and chip geometry are illustrative.

title: Weak Force Range — original explanatory diagram
author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. Using PDG 2024 W mass 80.3692 GeV/c² and NIST ℏc = 197.3269804 MeV fm gives ℏ/(mW c) ≈ 2.45526e-18 m. Curve is exp(-r/range), the exponential factor only, not the full Yukawa potential or a force measurement.

title: Muonic Hydrogen Atom — original explanatory diagram
author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. The FAMU paper states a ground-state muonic Bohr radius of about 285 fm, including proton–muon reduced mass. Twice this radius is approximately 570 fm = 0.57 pm. Cloud is schematic, not bounded at aμ, and the proton dot is enlarged. This diameter is a convention, not the full wavefunction extent.

title: Tau Compton Wavelength — original explanatory diagram
author: Universe Scales (original artwork)
changes: New original SVG; 1200 × 800 JPEG and 300 × 200 thumbnail. Ordinary (not reduced) Compton wavelength h/(mc), displayed as 0.698 fm, rounded from CODATA 2022. A single sine-wave glyph explains a length, with arbitrary amplitude; it is not a particle boundary, observed field oscillation, de Broglie wavelength or emitted-photon measurement.

title: Lolong skeleton at the National Museum of Natural History, Manila
author: Judgefloro
changes: Added subject/representation caption; Converted to JPEG at at most 1200 px image width; matching 300 px-wide thumbnail. Creator’s source page identifies the Lolong museum exhibit, including replica and skeleton, and explicitly dedicates the photograph under CC0. The selected frame visibly shows the suspended crocodile skeleton; the caption explicitly identifies a skeleton display rather than the living animal. No claim that photographic perspective measures his full 6.17 m body length.

title: AMNH titanosaur skeletal cast
author: D. Benjamin Miller
changes: Cropped downloaded source to [0, 0, 3000, 836]; Lifted shadows using gamma 0.78; Added subject/representation caption; Converted to JPEG at at most 1200 px image width; matching 300 px-wide thumbnail. Commons identifies this as the titanosaur skeleton cast at AMNH, photographed 18 January 2016, and the creator dedicates it under CC0. Used the original creator’s image, not the BY-SA derivative AMNHTitanosaur-03.jpg. Crop retains the visible head-to-tail cast and removes the separate fossil display on the right.

title: Individual sand grains through a microscope
author: Thelasthedgehog
changes: Cropped downloaded source to [130, 430, 830, 1230]; Added subject/representation caption; Converted to JPEG at at most 1200 px image width; matching 300 px-wide thumbnail. Source identifies microscopic observation of smooth sand and licenses the photograph CC BY 4.0. Crop isolates the resolved grains and excludes the dark eyepiece surroundings. No scale bar is invented; the pictured grains are not claimed to be exactly the representative 1 mm catalog size.

title: El Reno tornado in its multiple-vortex stage, 31 May 2013
author: Richard Thompson / NOAA Storm Prediction Center
changes: Converted to JPEG at at most 1200 px image width; matching 300 px-wide thumbnail. Commons describes the El Reno 31 May 2013 tornado in its multiple-vortex stage, credits Richard Thompson at SPC, and marks it PD-USGov. The image itself carries the event/date/SPC attribution. It shows the tornado, not the parent storm from orbit; visible funnels are not asserted to outline the maximum damage width.

title: Chloroplast cutaway illustration
author: DataBase Center for Life Science (DBCLS)
changes: Added subject/representation caption; Converted to JPEG at at most 1200 px image width; matching 300 px-wide thumbnail. Commons identifies an isolated chloroplast illustration by DBCLS, originally doi:10.7875/togopic.2017.50, under CC BY 4.0 with a completed license review. This is a teaching cutaway showing thylakoid stacks, not a micrograph or measured architecture.

title: Hunga Tonga eruption plume, Himawari-8, 15 January 2022 05:20 UTC
author: Japan Meteorological Agency (Himawari-8); Digital Typhoon / NII
changes: Selected animation frame 80 (zero-based); Added subject/representation caption; Converted to JPEG at at most 1200 px image width; matching 300 px-wide thumbnail. Source is the JMA / Digital Typhoon animation with explicit CC BY 4.0 terms, also linked to the compatible Japanese government data terms. Zero-based frame 80 visibly reads 2022-01-15 05:20:00 UTC and shows a large textured umbrella plume. Frame was fully decoded/composited by Pillow before export. Top-down view does not directly measure the plume’s height.

title: TRAPPIST-1 system versus the Solar System — orbit comparison
author: NASA, ESA, CSA, Joseph Olmsted (STScI)
changes: Converted to JPEG at at most 1200 px image width; matching 300 px-wide thumbnail. NASA’s asset caption explicitly identifies all seven planet orbits b–h and compares their compact orbital span with the inner Solar System. This is the 2026 orbital comparison diagram, not a travel poster or a literal photograph of exoplanets. NASA image-use guidance applies (the Hubble/Webb copyright pages redirect there); the asset has no third-party copyright notice.

title: Andromeda gaseous halo and 43 background-quasar sightlines — illustration
author: NASA, ESA, and E. Wheatley (STScI)

The source title says Illustration; the new caption preserves that distinction.
